In summary, our research is concerned with
the biodegradation of aged PAHs in a soil contaminated with coal-tar, which is an emerging environmental problem.
the development of a bioremediation approach for the remediation of a coal-tar contaminated soil using composting technology.
the bioremediation of aged PAH contaminated soil by in-vessel compost.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the biodegradation of PAHs in an aged coal tar contaminated soil amended with fresh compost can occur at temperatures as low as 38 degrees C.
in-vessel compost bioremediation of an older contaminated site is a more efficient approach to remediate aged PAH contaminated sites than the in-situ bioremediation approach.
the biodegradation of PAHs in a contaminated soil can be enhanced by adding a high quality green waste compost and by using an in-vessel compost bioreactor with a variable temperature profile.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a constant temperature profile at 38 degrees C is sufficient for biodegradation of PAHs in a soil amended with FGW.

in-vessel compost bioremediation of aged PAH-contaminated soil is possible, and that the process is enhanced by adding a fresh green waste compost and by using a constant temperature treatment at 38 degrees C.

in-vessel compost of a coal-tar-contamination soil amended with fresh compost at a TC1=38-55 degrees C for 56 days would be an efficient and economical approach for the bioremediation of aged PAH-contaminated soil.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the in-vessel compost-bioremediation approach is an effective method for the biodegradation of PAH-contaminated soil, but it is important to use a variable temperature profile to comply with regulatory standards for pathogen control.
the in-vessel compost-bioremediation process can be used to treat aged coal-tar soils and the bioremediation process could be optimized by selecting the appropriate composting temperature regime.

the use of fresh green waste as an amendment for in-vessel compost bioremediation of aged PAHs-contaminated soil may be a cost-effective alternative to the current practice of adding commercial composts to aged coal-tar contaminated soil for in-vessel bioremediation.
